messages:
maya: FYI i'm prototyping a keyboard-first quick-grant in the console. trigger: press 'g' when a principal is selected. goal = 1-tap grant for common presets. main concern: could this accidentally change routing/quotas silently? :thinking:
sam: we've seen customers hit unexpected routing fallbacks when entitlements changed unexpectedly. quick-grant needs the same preflight simulation + audit write as the full flow. no silent shortcuts.
li: yep. show an inline 'effective impact' summary (tiny sparkline or counts): routes affected, quota buckets touched. helps ops trust the shortcut.
jordan: also gate by enterprise policy. some tenants require approval for scopes that modify routing (e.g. any role with `route_admin`). if the shortcut touches those, open the full modal, not the quick flow.
maya: plan: maintain a small server-side sensitive_scopes list + client config. quick path checks it, and falls back to modal when matched. anyone concerned about added latency?
nora: simulate -> audit -> apply can add ~600-900ms. options: optimistic UI + revert on failure, or synchronous with clear spinner. Either way must show rollback affordance and record telemetry that grant failed and was reverted.
sam: telemetry shape proposal: fields = ["flow": quick_grant|modal, "sensitive_hit": true|false, "simulate_ok": true|false, "apply_latency_ms": number, "reverted": true|false]. include a sampled impacted_route_ids array (PII-safe) at 0.5-1% sampling.
li: add rollout_context to simulated payload so we can warn if a grant would affect active canaries. simulation should return warnings that the UI surfaces as a banner.
ops-bot: (ops-bot) deploy: feature flag `console.quick_grant_kb` enabled for staging.
maya: API proposal: reuse /authz/simulate then add an atomic grants endpoint that can run simulate+apply server-side: PATCH /authz/grants/atomic {"principal":"svc-123","roles":["viewer"],"apply_after_simulate":true}. server runs simulate, returns warnings/errors, and only applies if simulation unchanged. client gets single response.
sam: prefer server atomicity to avoid race windows. require the server to revalidate the simulation result with a short window (2s) and fail safe on diff.
jordan: also add X-Requested-By: console-quickgrant header so telemetry/ops can separate UI quick-grants vs API automation.
nora: tiny UX: keyboard hint should read "g — quick grant (Shift+G for full modal)" to surface the full flow. microcopy reduces surprise.
li: test plan: syrup tests for user, svc-account, role with route_admin, quota-affecting role. assert telemetry fields, audit entry, simulation warnings surfaced, and no silent routing drift.
maya: edge case: quick-grant during an active rollout. simulation should evaluate rollout context and warn or block if grant would re-route traffic to a blocked variant. i'll add rollout_context to simulate and surface warnings in the quick UI.
sam: another edge: if two engineers quick-grant different roles simultaneously to same principal, atomic apply must be serialized or return conflict. server should return 409 with current effective role set.
jordan: docs + changelog: call out the sensitive scopes list and how to request exceptions. operations teams should be able to extend the list per-tenant.
maya: i'll wire up prototype + telemetry schema + server flag gating. will open PR and ping for review. leaving open for any other edge cases. :eyes:
